scenarios.title: The Personal Trainer
scenarios.text: A private trainer who works with three Olympic athletes could change your whole offseason, for a price that makes your advisor wince. They have one opening.

choices.label: Hire the trainer
choices.result: Hired, for the summer. It's brutal and scientific, and you come back to camp faster, leaner and slightly afraid of the trainer.

choices.label: Ask for a trial week
choices.result: A trial week first. It's good, so you hire them for half the summer, and keep the other half for your own work.

choices.label: Train the way you always have
choices.result: Your own routine, the one that got you here. It's familiar and cheaper, and you wonder all summer what you're missing.

scenarios.title: Dinner With Influential People
scenarios.text: Your agent invites you to a private dinner with influential people in the league: two owners, a network executive and a former commissioner. Dress code: 'nice'.

choices.label: Be yourself
choices.result: Good stories, honestly told, and you laugh at your own mistakes. Two of the owners remember your name the next season.

choices.label: Mostly listen
choices.result: Mostly listening. You learn how the league actually works, who decides what and why, and you write it all down in the car.

choices.label: Skip the dinner
choices.result: No dinner. Your agent sighs and goes alone, and comes back with a story about you that isn't quite true.

scenarios.title: The Homecoming Event
scenarios.text: Your high school invites you back for its homecoming game. They want you at the pep rally, on the field at halftime, and in the trophy case photo with your old coach.

choices.label: Walk the halls with {parent}
choices.result: The halls, with {parent}, in the afternoon. A teacher still has your old essay about wanting to be a kicker, and reads it aloud.

choices.label: Talk to the team
choices.result: The football team before the game, in the old locker room. The kicker can't stop grinning, and you leave him your cleats.

choices.label: Send a halftime video
choices.result: A video, played at halftime on the old scoreboard. They cheer anyway, and someone films the crowd cheering for you and sends it.

scenarios.title: The Team's Future
scenarios.text: The franchise is talking about a full rebuild: younger, cheaper, faster. A reporter says there's a list of veterans who might be traded, and your name is on it.

choices.label: Make yourself essential
choices.result: The one veteran they can't rebuild without: that's the plan, and you work like it. The list changes by spring.

choices.label: Have your agent find out
choices.result: Your agent finds out which list it is. It's the good one, for now, and you breathe for the first time in a week.

choices.label: Invest in the young players
choices.result: The young players get your time, because they're the future and so, maybe, are you. The coaches notice who's helping.

scenarios.title: The New Family Responsibility
scenarios.text: A family member needs more of your time than the season has: {sibling} is going through a divorce, and calls every night after the kids are asleep.

choices.label: Make the time
choices.result: Flights on off days, calls every night. You're exhausted and present, and {sibling} says later that you were the reason they got through it.

choices.label: Build a plan with the family
choices.result: A family plan, so nobody carries it alone: {parent} takes Mondays, you take Thursdays, everyone takes Sunday. It works better than anyone hoped.

choices.label: Promise the offseason
choices.result: The offseason, promised, and kept. It's a long wait for both of you, and the calls in between are short.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Media Tour
scenarios.text: Your growing reputation comes with an offseason full of interview requests: podcasts, morning shows, and a magazine that wants to photograph you on a beach.

choices.label: Say yes to most
choices.result: Most of them, yes. Your name is everywhere by June, your phone never stops, and you're more tired than in season.

choices.label: Do three, and do them well
choices.result: Three interviews, carefully chosen and well prepared. One of them becomes the clip people share whenever your name comes up.

choices.label: Keep the summer quiet
choices.result: A quiet summer and your training, no interviews. Nobody photographs you on a beach, which suits you fine, and your agent sighs.

scenarios.title: The Career Milestone
scenarios.text: You reach a milestone and have to decide how to celebrate it.

choices.label: Celebrate with the specialists
choices.result: You take the specialists to dinner. {holder} gives a speech.

choices.label: Celebrate at home
choices.result: You celebrate at home with the people who knew you before.

choices.label: Thank the room
choices.result: You thank the whole room, one by one. It takes a while.

scenarios.title: The Fourth Season
scenarios.text: Your fourth pro season. Nobody calls you a rookie anymore, the equipment manager knows your cleat size by heart, and two of this year's rookies ask for your autograph.

choices.label: Look out for the rookies
choices.result: The rookies get looked after, the way someone once looked after you: rides, meals, the names of the people who matter.

choices.label: Raise your own bar
choices.result: Nobody else will raise your bar now, so you do it yourself: new goals, written down and taped to the bathroom mirror.

choices.label: Enjoy the ease
choices.result: Some ease, finally earned. You enjoy this season more than any before it, and the snapper says you look five years younger.

scenarios.title: The Comfortable Routine
scenarios.text: Your routine works so well it's starting to feel like a rut. Same breakfast, same warmup, same thoughts at the same moments. You haven't felt nervous in a month, and you miss it.

choices.label: Change one small thing
choices.result: One small change: a different song in your warmup. It's enough to wake you up, and your first kick that day feels new.

choices.label: Push harder inside it
choices.result: Harder, inside the exact same routine. It's tiring, and it works, and slowly the rut starts to feel like a groove again.

choices.label: Trust the rut
choices.result: A rut that works is a groove, you decide, and you trust it. The season goes on quietly and well.

scenarios.title: The Raise
scenarios.text: Your second contract is real money, and everyone you know has noticed: old friends with ideas, cousins with emergencies, a teacher from middle school with a fundraiser.

choices.label: Set one rule for everyone
choices.result: One rule, for everyone, written down. It's fair, it's a little lonely, and the calls slow down within a month.

choices.label: Help the ones who need it
choices.result: The people who really need it get help, quietly, and nobody else hears about it. {parent} finds out anyway and is proud.

choices.label: Change your number
choices.result: A new phone number, given to twelve people. Things get quieter immediately, and two old friends feel shut out and say so.

scenarios.title: The House With a Yard
scenarios.text: You buy a house with a backyard big enough for a kicking net. The previous owners left a swing set, a lemon tree and a note wishing you luck.

choices.label: Put up the net
choices.result: The net goes up the first weekend. The neighbors watch from their windows, and by Sunday their kids are shagging balls for you.

choices.label: Throw a housewarming
choices.result: Everyone, over, the first Saturday: family, teammates, neighbors. {parent} gives the tour twice, and {sibling} falls off the swing set.

choices.label: Sit under the lemon tree
choices.result: Nothing, in the backyard, under the lemon tree, for a whole afternoon. It's the first time in years you've done nothing on purpose.

scenarios.title: The Specialist Who Retires
scenarios.text: The punter you've worked beside for six years retires suddenly, with a two-line statement on a Tuesday afternoon. He hasn't returned anyone's calls since, including yours.

choices.label: Throw him a send-off
choices.result: A send-off with the specialists at his favorite diner, whether he likes it or not. He comes, finally, and it's loud and long.

choices.label: Help the new punter settle
choices.result: The new punter gets your time and the old punter's tricks, passed along. The unit stays steady through the change.

choices.label: Give him his quiet
choices.result: His quiet, respected. You send one short message and wait, and a month later he calls you first, from a lake.

scenarios.title: A Different Snap
scenarios.text: A new long snapper arrives, and for the first time in years your timing is off. The ball comes faster, flatter, with a spin you don't recognize, and the misses are in practice for everyone to see.

choices.label: Rep it out after practice
choices.result: After every practice, an extra fifty snaps until the timing is back. Your leg is heavy and your rhythm returns by week three.

choices.label: Get to know him first
choices.result: Off the field first: dinners, his family, his terrible music. The timing follows the trust, the way it always does, within two weeks.

choices.label: Film every snap
choices.result: Every snap, filmed and studied. You find the tenth of a second in the film room, and fix it in one afternoon.
